question: Should OpenClaw add a public `agents.list[].subagents.workspace` override for omitted-`agentId` native subagents, or keep explicit child agent profiles plus `requireAgentId`/`cwd` as the supported isolation model?
rationale: Source inspection proves the gap, but the change would create a new public config surface that controls child workspace bootstrap and file-access boundaries.

options.title: Keep Explicit Profiles
options.body: Preserve the current model where isolation uses configured child agent profiles, explicit `agentId`, and `requireAgentId`, with docs or diagnostics improvements if needed.

options.title: Add Narrow Opt-In Config
options.body: Approve `subagents.workspace` only as a strict same-agent default-child override with schema, docs, doctor/security review, and focused workspace tests.

options.title: Defer To Broader Workdir Design
options.body: Hold this until the broader subagent workdir and skill isolation discussion in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/87253 is resolved.

recommendation.title: Keep Explicit Profiles
recommendation.body: Preserve the current model where isolation uses configured child agent profiles, explicit `agentId`, and `requireAgentId`, with docs or diagnostics improvements if needed.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent workspace-boundary hardening makes this the closest available owner for deciding whether the public config surface is acceptable.
